page: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v7 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs based on the arm64 architecture and 384 GB of memory, delivering a balanced ratio of 4 GB per core. The server does not contain dedicated graphics hardware.

Integrated directly into the instance is 5670 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage tiers. Because it relies on the arm64 instruction set, workloads require ARM software support, and traditional x86 CPU extensions such as AVX or AMX are not supported.

The instance delivers strong qualitative resource efficiency by pairing high processor density with extensive fast NVMe local storage, avoiding the overhead of external disk communication for temporary data. Best-fit workloads include multi-threaded application servers, distributed databases requiring rapid scratch disks, continuous integration build clusters, and large-scale batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v7 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 96 dedicated arm64 vCPUs and 384 GB of system RAM under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual processor, making it well-balanced for diverse computing tasks. It includes 5670 GB of high-performance local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage, providing ample fast disk capacity for low-latency scratch space. The architecture does not incorporate discrete GPUs and requires applications compiled for 64-bit ARM environments. In terms of cost efficiency, the dense core count combined with integrated NVMe capacity reduces dependency on network storage for temporary IOPS-heavy operations. The instance is suited for large database deployments, enterprise application runtimes, compilation pipelines, and data ingestion services.
